groups.title: Who should employees contact about each problem?
groups.instruction: Choose FIVE answers from the box and write the correct letter, A–F, next to Questions 16–20.

parts.context: An HR officer gives an induction talk to new warehouse employees.

transcript.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Eastway Distribution. I'm Ms Grey from the human resources department, and over the next ten minutes I'll cover the essentials you need to know before you start your first shift.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: Let me begin with working hours. Most staff work an eight-hour shift with a one-hour break. You'll be told your pattern at the end of this session, but the early shift starts at six, not at seven as it says on your contracts, because we recently changed it.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: A word of advice: please arrive a little before your shift starts, because you need time to change, collect your equipment and get to your area.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: You will all be given a locker for your belongings. The code is chosen by you, and I'd recommend not using your birthday, because it's the first thing people try. Mobile phones must be kept in the locker while you are on the warehouse floor.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: For safety, you must wear a high-visibility jacket and safety boots. The company provides both, but you're responsible for keeping them clean. If you lose them, a replacement will be deducted from your pay.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: Training is very important to us. In your first week you'll complete a one-day safety course, and later in the year there are optional courses on forklift driving. These are popular, so places fill quickly.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: Forklift driving, in particular, can lead to a pay rise, so the company encourages people who are interested to apply as soon as they have completed their probation period.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: Now I'd like to explain who to contact if you have a problem. If you have a question about protective equipment or an accident, you should speak to Ms Ito, the health and safety officer. Her office is next to the canteen.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: If you want to request a holiday, don't come to HR. Your shift manager, Dan, approves all leave requests, and he asks for at least two weeks' notice, except in an emergency.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: If your payslip looks wrong, or you haven't been paid on time, contact Mr Hall in payroll. He's very efficient, but he's only in the office on Tuesdays and Thursdays, so send an email on other days.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: For computer problems, such as a forgotten login, ring the IT helpdesk. They are on extension two-two-one, and they can usually reset a password within a few minutes.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: And if you're interested in a training course, or you want to develop your career, speak to Ms Park in the training department. She can explain which courses are paid for by the company.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: One final point on communication. Notices are put on the board by the canteen, but important changes are also sent by text message, so please make sure we have your correct number.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: I'd also encourage you to read the staff handbook carefully, as it explains many other rules about behaviour, dress and attendance that I have no time to cover today.
transcript.speaker: MS GREY

transcript.text: Welcome again, and I hope you'll enjoy working here. Does anyone have any questions before we start the tour?
transcript.speaker: MS GREY
